messages:
marta_docs: Heads-up — I'm landing a PR that consolidates Dedicated capacity docs. Main changes: a step-by-step provisioning checklist, two autoscaling policy examples (conservative + aggressive), clearer SLA language, a short migration note from Dedicated -> Private, and Node/Python SDK snippets. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pulls/4822

ben_infra: Nice. Can you call out the required IAM roles and the network isolation section? we should be explicit about VPC peering vs Private deployment network boundaries.

marta_docs: Yep — added an 'isolation considerations' subsection. It currently says "Dedicated pools are logically isolated; for strict network isolation use Private with customer VPC". Want wording suggestions on the SLA bullet.

sam_eng: SLA wording: avoid hard numbers unless Legal signs off. Suggest: "We target X ms p50 and Y ms p95 per model class under reserved capacity; see Dedicated SLAs page for contract details." Link to SLA page?

marta_docs: Good point. I changed to: "Target latency and availability are defined by committed Dedicated contracts; refer to the SLA summary (link) for metrics and remedies." Still need a real link — left a TODO.

ashley_support: Also add the support matrix (what team to ping for on-call vs account manager). A quick table helps — even 3 rows: provisioning, performance, billing.

oliver_sdk: I added two SDK snippets in the PR: Node example to create a dedicated pool and Python example to set an autoscale policy. Posting them here for review:

oliver_sdk: ```js
// Node: create dedicated pool
const rd = require('@redwood/inference');
await rd.dedicated.createPool({
  name: 'prod-pool-a',
  region: 'us-west-2',
  instanceType: 'a100-40gb',
  minReplicas: 2,
  maxReplicas: 8,
});
```

oliver_sdk: ```py
# Python: update autoscale policy
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient(api_key=ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'])
client.update_autoscale('pool-prod-a', autoscale={
  'target_tokens_per_sec': 40000,
  'cooldown_seconds': 120,
  'scale_up_increment': 1,
})
```

jen_review: Snippets look fine. Minor nit: in the Node snippet, show await rd.auth or client init so it's copy-paste friendly. In Python, maybe show exception handling for quota errors.

marta_docs: Will add those. Also need eyes on the autoscale example YAML I added under "Policy examples" — conservative vs aggressive. Ben, can you confirm the conservative defaults for GPU-backed pools?

ben_infra: Conservative defaults look OK but recommend bumping cooldown to 180s for large models to avoid thrashing. Also note that for multi-tenant Dedicated pools, prefix caching is disabled by default (callout in docs).

marta_docs: Done — increased cooldown and added note about prefix cache behavior. Also replaced the TODO SLA link with https://intranet.redwood.com/legal/sla-summary (internal).

sam_eng: One more: the migration note from Dedicated -> Private should list steps to export routing policies, revoke shared credentials, and coordinate downtime window. Maybe a checklist with minimal outage strategy.

marta_docs: Added short checklist and a sample maintenance plan. I'll include the template maintenance-notice snippet we use for customers.

ashley_support: Quick fix: the diagram link in "isolation architecture" 404s. I think the correct path is /assets/diagrams/dedicated-vs-private.svg.

marta_docs: Thanks — fixed link.

deploy-bot: CI: docs-lint passed. spellcheck found 1 suggestion in docs/dedicated/provisioning.md ("teh" -> "the").

marta_docs: Addressed spelling. PR updated: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pulls/4822 (now includes SDK init lines, exception handling notes, updated autoscale cooldowns, SLA link, and diagram fix).

jen_review: I'll do a final pass this afternoon, primarily the SLA wording and the migration checklist clarity. If I don't get to it by EOD, feel free to merge the docs-only PR and open a follow-up for any legal wording changes.

marta_docs: Cool. Plan: merge after Jen's review or EOD if no blockers. Tagging @ben_infra and @oliver_sdk for follow-up on code samples once merged. :thumbsup:
